stories.headline: Alibaba Releases Qwen3.6-27B, a Dense Model That Outperforms Its Own 397B MoE on Coding Benchmarks

key_facts.fact: Qwen3.6-27B is a 27-billion-parameter dense open-weight model under Apache 2.0 license, the first dense variant in the Qwen 3.6 family.
key_facts.excerpt: Alibaba's Qwen Team has released Qwen3.6-27B, the first dense open-weight model in the Qwen3.6 family — and arguably the most capable 27-billion-parameter model available today for coding agents.

key_facts.fact: On SWE-bench Verified the model scores 77.2%, surpassing the much larger Qwen3.5-397B-A17B MoE (which scored lower) and approaching Claude 4.5 Opus's 80.9%.
key_facts.excerpt: SWE-bench Verified scores 77.2, up from 75.0, and competitive with Claude 4.5 Opus's 80.9.

key_facts.fact: On Terminal-Bench 2.0, Qwen3.6-27B scores 59.3, matching Claude 4.5 Opus exactly and far exceeding the 35B MoE sibling's 51.5.
key_facts.excerpt: Terminal-Bench 2.0, evaluated under a 3-hour timeout with 32 CPUs and 48 GB RAM, reaches 59.3 — matching Claude 4.5 Opus exactly, and outperforming Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (51.5).

key_facts.fact: The model uses a hybrid architecture blending Gated DeltaNet linear attention with traditional self-attention, supporting 262K native context (extendable to 1M tokens via YaRN).
key_facts.excerpt: Native context is 262,144 tokens; YaRN scaling is advertised up to 1,010,000 tokens for experimental long-document jobs.

key_facts.fact: It introduces a Thinking Preservation mechanism that keeps prior chain-of-thought across turns so the model doesn't re-derive scratch work each tool round.
key_facts.excerpt: For multi-turn agents, the release introduces thinking preservation—an API/template flag that keeps earlier chain-of-thought blocks in the visible history.

key_facts.fact: On reasoning benchmarks GPQA Diamond reaches 87.8, AIME 2026 hits 94.1, and LiveCodeBench v6 scores 83.9.
key_facts.excerpt: On reasoning benchmarks, GPQA Diamond reaches 87.8 (up from 85.5), AIME26 hits 94.1 (up from 92.6), and LiveCodeBench v6 scores 83.9 (up from 80.7).

stories.headline: OpenAI Launches Workspace Agents in ChatGPT, Replacing Custom GPTs With Codex-Powered Automation

key_facts.fact: OpenAI introduced workspace agents in ChatGPT, Codex-powered shared agents that can handle complex, multi-step, long-running workflows across connected tools like Slack, Salesforce, and Notion.
key_facts.excerpt: Workspace agents are an evolution of GPTs. Powered by Codex, they can take on many of the tasks people already do at work—from preparing reports, to writing code, to responding to messages.

key_facts.fact: Workspace agents run in the cloud and continue working even when users are offline, and are designed to be shared within an organization.
key_facts.excerpt: They run in the cloud, so they can keep working even when you're not. They're also designed to be shared within an organization, so teams can build an agent once, use it together in ChatGPT or Slack.

key_facts.fact: The feature is available as a research preview for ChatGPT Business, Enterprise, Edu, and Teachers plans, free until May 6 when credit-based pricing begins.
key_facts.excerpt: Workspace agents are currently available in research preview for ChatGPT Business, Enterprise, Edu and Teachers plans. OpenAI said the feature will remain free until May 6, 2026, after which it will move to a credit-based pricing model.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI will make it possible to convert existing custom GPTs directly into workspace agents in the future.
key_facts.excerpt: In the future, OpenAI will also make it possible to convert custom GPTs directly into workspace agents.

key_facts.fact: Early adopter Rippling reports 70% time savings on recurring sales workflows, reducing manual effort from 5-6 hours/week to background automation.
key_facts.excerpt: Early adopters like Rippling report 70% time savings on recurring sales workflows, reducing manual effort from 5–6 hours/week to background automation.

stories.headline: OpenAI Releases Privacy Filter, an Open-Weight Model for PII Detection With 1.5B Parameters

key_facts.fact: Privacy Filter is an open-weight model with 1.5 billion total parameters and 50 million active parameters, released under Apache 2.0 on Hugging Face and GitHub.
key_facts.excerpt: With 1.5 billion total parameters and 50 million active parameters, Privacy Filter identifies private names, addresses, email addresses, phone numbers, URLs, dates, account numbers, passwords, API keys, and other sensitive information.

key_facts.fact: The model processes up to 128,000 tokens in a single forward pass and is small enough to run on a standard laptop or in a web browser.
key_facts.excerpt: By providing a 1.5-billion-parameter model that can run on a standard laptop or directly in a web browser, the company is effectively handing developers a 'privacy-by-design' toolkit.

key_facts.fact: It uses a sparse MoE bidirectional token-classification architecture (described as a 'Mixture of BERTs') derived from the gpt-oss family.
key_facts.excerpt: Architecturally, Privacy Filter is a derivative of OpenAI's gpt-oss family, a series of open-weight reasoning models.

key_facts.fact: The model scored 96% on the PII-Masking-300k benchmark out of the box, rising to 97.43% with a corrected version of the test.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI reports its model scored 96% on a standard benchmark using the PII-Masking-300k dataset out of the box, with a corrected version of the same test pushing it to 97.43%.

key_facts.fact: It detects eight PII categories: names, addresses, emails, phone numbers, URLs, dates, account numbers, and secrets like passwords and API keys.
key_facts.excerpt: Privacy Filter scans for eight categories of personal information: names, addresses, emails, phone numbers, URLs, dates, account numbers, and secrets like passwords and API keys.

stories.headline: Tencent Releases Hy3-Preview, First Flagship AI Model Under Former OpenAI Researcher Yao Shunyu

key_facts.fact: Tencent released and open-sourced Hy3-preview (Hunyuan 3.0 Preview), a MoE language model with 295B total parameters, 21B activated parameters, and 256K max context length.
key_facts.excerpt: Hy3 preview is a MoE language model integrating fast and slow thinking, with 295 billion total parameters, 21 billion activated parameters, and support for a maximum context length of 256K.

key_facts.fact: The model is smaller than Tencent's previous flagship HY 2.0 (400B+ parameters), reflecting a focus on balancing performance and cost-effectiveness rather than pursuing massive scale.
key_facts.excerpt: The model is relatively small with only 295 billion parameters, bucking a recent trend of large models with trillions of parameters.

key_facts.fact: It is the first model since former OpenAI researcher Yao Shunyu joined Tencent as Chief AI Scientist; training began in late January 2026 and took less than three months.
key_facts.excerpt: Hy3 preview is not only the first large model after Hunyuan underwent a full-link reconstruction but also Yao Shunyu's first report card since joining Tencent as Chief AI Scientist.

key_facts.fact: On SWE-Bench coding benchmarks, Hy3-preview scored 74.4%, up from Hy2's 53.0%, a more than 40% improvement in coding capability.
key_facts.excerpt: Hy2在这个测试中只有53.0%的分数，Hy3 preview提升到了74.4%，编程能力猛增了40%以上

key_facts.fact: Tencent says agentic capabilities were one of the most significantly improved areas; the model has been deployed in Yuanbao, CodeBuddy, and other internal Tencent products.
key_facts.excerpt: Agentic capabilities were 'one of the most significantly improved areas in this release'... the model was already deployed in Tencent's flagship AI products including consumer app Yuanbao and coding assistant CodeBuddy.

key_facts.fact: Yao Shunyu stated Hy3-preview is the first step in reconstructing the Hunyuan large model, and a larger model is already in development.
key_facts.excerpt: Yao Shunyu stated that Hy3 preview is the first step in reconstructing the Hunyuan large model... under the support of new infrastructure and technical philosophy, Hunyuan's larger models are already on the way.

stories.headline: DeepSeek Seeks $20B+ Valuation in First Outside Funding Round as Tencent and Alibaba Vie to Invest

key_facts.fact: DeepSeek is in talks with Tencent and Alibaba for its first-ever external funding round, targeting a valuation of more than $20 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: Tencent and Alibaba are in talks to invest in DeepSeek as the AI startup pursues its first outside funding round at a valuation north of $20 billion, according to a report by The Information.

key_facts.fact: The target valuation doubled from initial discussions last week of at least $10 billion, as investor interest surged; the company is seeking to raise at least $300 million.
key_facts.excerpt: The Information first broke the news Friday that DeepSeek has begun talks to raise outside capital for the first time, aiming to secure at least $300 million at a valuation of $10 billion or more.

key_facts.fact: DeepSeek has relied entirely on backing from parent company High-Flyer Capital Management until now, with its models fully open-source and consumer chatbot free, generating no substantial revenue.
key_facts.excerpt: The company is seeking to raise at least $300 million, marking a sharp shift for a startup that has so far relied entirely on backing from its parent, High-Flyer Capital Management.

key_facts.fact: The fundraise comes as DeepSeek faces talent departures (core researcher Luo Fuli joined Xiaomi's MiMo team) and delays to its flagship V4 model originally planned for February.
key_facts.excerpt: 近期已有多位DeepSeek核心研究員遭到高薪挖角跳槽至中國國內大廠，例如骨幹成員Luo Fuli已正式加入小米... 原訂於今年2月發布的新一代旗艦模型V4，因面臨棘手的工程挑戰，時間表已屢遭推遲。

key_facts.fact: Some US venture capital firms are cautious about investing because DeepSeek is a Chinese startup, while competitors MiniMax and Zhipu have already gone public in Hong Kong.
key_facts.excerpt: Some U.S. venture capital firms are taking a cautious stance because it is a Chinese startup.

stories.headline: OpenAI Launches Free ChatGPT for Clinicians With Frontier Models and HealthBench Professional

key_facts.fact: ChatGPT for Clinicians is free for verified US physicians, nurse practitioners, physician assistants, and pharmacists, offering access to frontier models for clinical workflows.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI today released ChatGPT for Clinicians, a free tool for verified U.S. physicians, nurse practitioners, physician assistants and pharmacists.

key_facts.fact: The tool includes trusted clinical search citing millions of peer-reviewed sources, deep journal research that compiles cited reports in minutes, and skills for repeatable workflows like referral letters and prior authorizations.
key_facts.excerpt: Trusted clinical search: Reason through cases faster with real-time, cited answers based on evidence from millions of reputable, peer-reviewed medical sources.

key_facts.fact: Physician advisors reviewed 6,924 conversations and deemed 99.6% of responses safe and accurate; HIPAA support is available through a Business Associate Agreement.
key_facts.excerpt: Physician advisors reviewed 6,924 conversations; 99.6% of responses were deemed safe and accurate.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI also launched HealthBench Professional, an open benchmark for evaluating AI on real clinician tasks; GPT-5.4 in the Clinicians workspace outperformed other models and human physicians.
key_facts.excerpt: HealthBench Professional also arrives as an open benchmark... In trials, GPT‑5.4 in the Clinicians workspace outperformed base GPT‑5.4, other models and human physicians.

key_facts.fact: A 2026 AMA survey found 72% of physicians now use AI in clinical practice, up from 48% the prior year, with weekly usage more than doubled.
key_facts.excerpt: A 2026 survey by the American Medical Association found that 72 per cent of physicians now use AI in clinical practice, up from 48 per cent the previous year.

key_facts.fact: Clinical research activities can earn CME credits automatically, and OpenAI plans to expand access internationally through the Better Evidence Network.
key_facts.excerpt: As you research clinical questions in ChatGPT, an eligible evidence review can automatically count toward continuing medical education credits.

stories.headline: China's 360 Digital Security Uses AI Agent to Discover ~1,000 Unknown Software Vulnerabilities

key_facts.fact: 360 Digital Security Group developed an AI-powered 'Vulnerability Discovery Agent' that uncovered approximately 1,000 previously unknown vulnerabilities, including in Microsoft Office and OpenClaw.
key_facts.excerpt: Chinese cybersecurity firm 360 Digital Security Group has used an artificial intelligence agent to uncover approximately 1,000 previously unknown software vulnerabilities, including critical flaws embedded deep within Microsoft Office applications.

key_facts.fact: The AI agent used a combination of LLM reasoning, symbolic execution, and reinforcement learning to explore software behavior, finding flaws in memory handling, input validation, and privilege escalation over a six-month testing window.
key_facts.excerpt: 360's AI agent used a combination of large language model (LLM) reasoning, symbolic execution, and reinforcement learning to explore software behavior at machine speed.

key_facts.fact: The findings were detailed in a report by Natto Thoughts, a research group focused on Chinese cybersecurity, positioning 360 as a competitor to Anthropic's Mythos in AI-driven vulnerability discovery.
key_facts.excerpt: A large Chinese cybersecurity firm is using artificial intelligence to identify security vulnerabilities in widely used software applications, positioning itself as a competitor to Anthropic.

key_facts.fact: 360 says the agent operates under strict ethical constraints: no live exploitation, no data exfiltration, and testing conducted in isolated, air-gapped environments.
key_facts.excerpt: The company emphasizes that its AI agent operates under strict ethical constraints, including no live exploitation, no data exfiltration, and testing conducted in isolated, air-gapped environments.

key_facts.fact: The system reduces vulnerability detection time from weeks to hours, operating continuously and autonomously unlike traditional penetration testing.
key_facts.excerpt: This AI-driven approach operates continuously and autonomously, reducing detection time from weeks to hours.
